categories.heading: Our disciplines
categories.intro: Our academy trains Jiu-Jitsu end to end: from your very first grip on the mat to the competition podium, through a method that blends technique, discipline and community.

cards.title: Gi Jiu-Jitsu
cards.description: The traditional art, trained in the kimono. Collar and sleeve grips open up a rich game of control, sweeps and submissions built on patience and technique.
cards.more: Gi classes emphasise grip fighting, guard retention and the fundamentals that carry over to every level. Ideal if you want a deep, methodical understanding of Jiu-Jitsu — from your first day to your black belt.

cards.title: No-Gi Grappling
cards.description: Fast, dynamic and slippery. Without the kimono the game speeds up, rewarding pressure, body control and a relentless pace on the mat.
cards.more: No-Gi focuses on underhooks, body locks and wrestling-based control, with a game that translates directly to competition and MMA. A great complement to Gi or a discipline in its own right.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Everything you need to know about the academy and how it works. Can't find your answer? Get in touch and we'll help.

questions.question: What's the minimum age for kids to train?
questions.answer: We welcome kids from age 4. Classes are split by age and level so every group trains safely and in a way that suits their development.

questions.question: Is Jiu-Jitsu safe for children?
questions.answer: Yes. BJJ is a control-based martial art with no striking, and our kids' classes prioritise technique, respect and play. Coaches supervise every session closely.

questions.question: What do children learn in class?
questions.answer: Beyond technique, we work on discipline, coordination, confidence and teamwork. Many families notice better focus and self-esteem within the first few weeks.

questions.question: Do I need to buy a kimono to start?
questions.answer: You don't need anything for your first trial class: we lend you the gear. If you decide to stay, we'll help you pick your first kimono (Gi) at the best price.

questions.question: What's the difference between Gi and No-Gi?
questions.answer: The Gi is the traditional kimono and opens up a collar and sleeve grip game. No-Gi is trained in a rashguard and shorts, faster and more dynamic. You can practise both.

questions.question: What should I bring to each class?
questions.answer: A clean kimono (or rashguard and shorts for No-Gi), a water bottle and sandals for moving off the mat. Hygiene matters: short nails and clean kit, always.

questions.question: What's the training methodology like?
questions.answer: We combine technique, positional sparring and progressive rolling. Each class has a clear goal and difficulty adapts to your level, from beginner to competitor.

questions.question: I've never done contact sports, can I start?
questions.answer: Absolutely. Everyone starts from zero someday. Classes are open to everyone and we adapt the intensity to each person regardless of your starting point.

questions.question: How often should I train to progress?
questions.answer: With two or three sessions a week you'll see steady progress. Consistency is what matters: little and often beats a lot every now and then.

questions.question: How do I book my free trial class?
questions.answer: Message us through the contact form or WhatsApp and we'll assign you a slot. Your first class is free and with no commitment.

questions.question: Do I book every class or is it open schedule?
questions.answer: With your membership you can attend your group's classes within the weekly schedule. For special events, seminars or trial classes we do ask you to book in advance.

questions.question: Can I cancel or change my booking?
questions.answer: Yes. If you can't make it, let us know in advance and we'll reschedule your session, no problem.

questions.question: Where is the academy and what are the hours?
questions.answer: We're at the Presa training centre. Check the schedule section on this page to see all the available Kids and Adults time slots.

questions.question: How much is the monthly membership?
questions.answer: We have several options depending on your training days. Check the pricing section or message us for the up-to-date details and the best fit for you.

questions.question: Do you offer adult and competition classes?
questions.answer: Yes. We have groups for every level, from beginners to a competition team that represents Presa at national and international tournaments.
